title: Theaters

description.main: The third volume in the Damiani and Matsumoto Editions series on Hiroshi Sugimoto, collecting 130 photographs from the Theaters series he began in the late 1970s, 18 of them published here for the first time. Text by the artist, designed by Takaaki Matsumoto. Clothbound with dust jacket, 176 pages.
description.extended:
Hiroshi Sugimoto's Theaters, the third volume in the Damiani and Matsumoto Editions series on his work, collects 130 photographs from the series he began in the late 1970s, 18 of them published here for the first time.

The premise, in Sugimoto's words, was to shoot a whole movie in a single frame. He sets a large-format camera in an auditorium and opens the shutter when the film starts and closes it when it ends. There is no light but the projection. The screen records as a white rectangle, and its glow draws the surrounding architecture out of the dark. He began with the American movie palaces of the 1920s and 1930s and went on to drive-ins. In the last decade he has photographed historic theatres in Europe and abandoned cinemas decaying around the screen. The 176-page clothbound book has a dust jacket and was designed by Takaaki Matsumoto. In his text Sugimoto recalls his first exposure in the series as an image no one had seen, one that existed nowhere but in the camera.

Sugimoto (b. 1948, Tokyo) has worked between Tokyo and New York since the 1970s. His work is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art, Tate and the National Museum of Modern Art, Tokyo. The Theaters share their long exposures with the Seascapes and Dioramas, published in the same format in 2015 and 2014. Damiani reissued Theaters in 2026 under the same ISBN.
description.artist_bio: Hiroshi Sugimoto (b. 1948, Tokyo) moved to New York in 1974 and divides his time between Tokyo and New York. His work is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo, the National Gallery London, the National Museum of Modern Art Tokyo, the Smithsonian and Tate (per Artbook/D.A.P.).

notes: Shelf: Japanese. Damiani / Matsumoto Editions series. Third volume in the series (Dioramas 2014, Seascapes 2015). First printing 2016; 130 black-and-white photographs, 18 previously unpublished; designed by Takaaki Matsumoto; text by the artist. Damiani reissued the book in August 2026 under the same ISBN (its product page now carries the reprint); the shelf copy is taken to be the 2016 printing. Damiani lists the original release as August 2016; US release through Artbook/D.A.P. September 2016.
